        "originalContents": "\n\n/**\n * Maps a URL using the provided payload and configuration.\n * @param {MapRequest} payload - The payload containing map parameters.\n * @param {Partial\u003cFirecrawlConfig\u003e} [config={}] - Optional configuration overrides.\n * @returns The response of the map operation.\n */\nexport async function mapUrl(\n  payload: MapRequest,\n  config: Partial\u003cFirecrawlConfig\u003e = {}\n) {\n  try {\n    const validatedPayload = mapUrlInputSchema.parse(payload);\n    const mergedConfig = { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG, ...config };\n    const app = initializeFirecrawl();\n\n    const mapOptions = {\n      limit: validatedPayload.limit ?? 10,\n    };\n\n    const response = await executeWithRetry(\n      () =\u003e app.mapUrl(validatedPayload.url, mapOptions),\n      \"Map\",\n      { url: validatedPayload.url },\n      mergedConfig\n    );\n\n    if (!response.success) {\n      throw new Error(\"Map operation failed\");\n    }\n\n    return response as FireCrawlResponse\u003cFirecrawlAction.Map\u003e;\n  } catch (error) {\n    return handleError(error, {\n      action: FirecrawlAction.Map,\n      properties: payload,\n    });\n  }\n}",

        "contents": "\n\n/**\n * Crawls a URL using the provided payload and configuration.\n * @param {CrawlRequest} payload - The payload containing crawl parameters.\n * @param {Partial\u003cFirecrawlConfig\u003e} [config={}] - Optional configuration overrides.\n * @returns The response of the crawl operation.\n */\nexport async function crawlUrl(\n  payload: CrawlRequest,\n  config: Partial\u003cFirecrawlConfig\u003e = {}\n) {\n  try {\n    const validatedPayload = crawlUrlInputSchema.parse(payload);\n    const mergedConfig = { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG, ...config };\n    const app = initializeFirecrawl();\n\n    const crawlOptions = {\n      maxDepth: validatedPayload.maxDepth ?? 1,\n      limit: validatedPayload.limit ?? 10,\n      allowBackwardLinks: validatedPayload.allowBackwardLinks ?? false,\n      allowExternalLinks: validatedPayload.allowExternalLinks ?? false,\n      ignoreSitemap: validatedPayload.ignoreSitemap ?? false,\n      scrapeOptions: {\n        waitFor: validatedPayload.waitFor ?? mergedConfig.defaultWaitTime,\n        formats: validatedPayload.formats,\n      },\n    };\n\n    const response = await executeWithRetry(\n      () =\u003e app.crawlUrl(validatedPayload.url, crawlOptions),\n      \"Crawl\",\n      { url: validatedPayload.url },\n      mergedConfig\n    );\n\n    if (!response.success) {\n      throw new Error(\"Crawl operation failed\");\n    }\n\n    return response as FireCrawlResponse\u003cFirecrawlAction.Crawl\u003e;\n  } catch (error) {\n    return handleError(error, {\n      action: FirecrawlAction.Crawl,\n      properties: payload,\n    });\n  }\n}",

        "contents": "\n\n/**\n * Scrapes a URL using the provided payload and configuration.\n * @param {ScrapeRequest} payload - The payload containing scrape parameters.\n * @param {Partial\u003cFirecrawlConfig\u003e} [config={}] - Optional configuration overrides.\n * @returns The response of the scrape operation.\n */\nexport async function scrapeUrl(\n  payload: ScrapeRequest,\n  config: Partial\u003cFirecrawlConfig\u003e = {}\n) {\n  try {\n    const validatedPayload = scrapeInputSchema.parse(payload);\n    const mergedConfig = { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG, ...config };\n    const app = initializeFirecrawl();\n\n    const scrapeOptions = {\n      waitFor: validatedPayload.waitFor ?? mergedConfig.defaultWaitTime,\n      formats: validatedPayload.formats,\n      extract: validatedPayload.formats.includes(\"extract\")\n        ? {\n            systemPrompt: validatedPayload.systemPrompt,\n            prompt: validatedPayload.prompt,\n          }\n        : undefined,\n    };\n\n    const response = await executeWithRetry(\n      () =\u003e app.scrapeUrl(validatedPayload.url, scrapeOptions),\n      \"Scrape\",\n      { url: validatedPayload.url },\n      mergedConfig\n    );\n\n    if (!response.success) {\n      throw new Error(\"Scrape operation failed\");\n    }\n\n    return response as FireCrawlResponse\u003cFirecrawlAction.Scrape\u003e;\n  } catch (error) {\n    return handleError(error, {\n      action: FirecrawlAction.Scrape,\n      properties: payload,\n    });\n  }\n}",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "# Model Context Protocol (MCP)\n\nThe Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that enables developers to build secure, two-way connections between their data sources and AI-powered tools. It standardizes how applications provide context and tools to Large Language Models (LLMs).\n\n## What is MCP?\n\nMCP functions as a plugin system for AI applications like Cursor, Claude, and Windsurf. It allows you to extend an AI agent's capabilities by connecting it to various data sources and tools through standardized interfaces.\n\nThink of MCP as a bridge between AI assistants and the systems where data lives, including:\n- Content repositories\n- Business tools\n- Development environments\n- Local file systems\n- APIs and databases\n\nMCP servers can be written in any language that can print to &#96;stdout&#96; or serve an HTTP endpoint, making it flexible and accessible for developers regardless of their preferred technology stack.\n\n## Architecture\n\nMCP uses a client-server architecture:\n\n1. **MCP Servers**: Provide data and functionality to AI tools\n2. **MCP Clients**: AI applications (like Cursor) that connect to MCP servers\n\nCursor supports two transport types for MCP servers:\n\n### 💻 stdio Transport\n- Runs on your **local machine**\n- Managed automatically by Cursor\n- Communicates directly via &#96;stdout&#96;\n- Only accessible by you locally\n\n**Input:** Valid shell command that is run by Cursor automatically\n\n### 🌐 SSE Transport\n- Can run **locally or remotely**\n- Managed and run by you\n- Communicates **over the network**\n- Can be **shared** across machines\n\n**Input:** URL to the &#96;/sse&#96; endpoint of an MCP server external to Cursor\n\n## Configuring MCP Servers\n\nMCP servers are configured using JSON files. You can place this configuration in two locations:\n\n### Project Configuration\nFor tools specific to a project, create a &#96;.cursor/mcp.json&#96; file in your project directory. This allows you to define MCP servers that are only available within that specific project.\n\n",
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "lineNumber": 1,
            "text": "# Model Context Protocol (MCP)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3,
            "text": "The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that enables developers to build secure, two-way connections between their data sources and AI-powered tools. It standardizes how applications provide context and tools to Large Language Models (LLMs)."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4
          },
          {

        "originalContents": "# Model Context Protocol (MCP)\n\nThe Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that enables developers to build secure, two-way connections between their data sources and AI-powered tools. It standardizes how applications provide context and tools to Large Language Models (LLMs).\n\n## What is MCP?\n\nMCP functions as a plugin system for AI applications like Cursor, Claude, and Windsurf. It allows you to extend an AI agent's capabilities by connecting it to various data sources and tools through standardized interfaces.\n\nThink of MCP as a bridge between AI assistants and the systems where data lives, including:\n- Content repositories\n- Business tools\n- Development environments\n- Local file systems\n- APIs and databases\n\nMCP servers can be written in any language that can print to &#96;stdout&#96; or serve an HTTP endpoint, making it flexible and accessible for developers regardless of their preferred technology stack.\n\n## Architecture\n\nMCP uses a client-server architecture:\n\n1. **MCP Servers**: Provide data and functionality to AI tools\n2. **MCP Clients**: AI applications (like Cursor) that connect to MCP servers\n\nCursor supports two transport types for MCP servers:\n\n### 💻 stdio Transport\n- Runs on your **local machine**\n- Managed automatically by Cursor\n- Communicates directly via &#96;stdout&#96;\n- Only accessible by you locally\n\n**Input:** Valid shell command that is run by Cursor automatically\n\n### 🌐 SSE Transport\n- Can run **locally or remotely**\n- Managed and run by you\n- Communicates **over the network**\n- Can be **shared** across machines\n\n**Input:** URL to the &#96;/sse&#96; endpoint of an MCP server external to Cursor\n\n## Configuring MCP Servers\n\nMCP servers are configured using JSON files. You can place this configuration in two locations:\n\n### Project Configuration\nFor tools specific to a project, create a &#96;.cursor/mcp.json&#96; file in your project directory. This allows you to define MCP servers that are only available within that specific project.\n\n",

        "contents": "\n    \n    # Initialize MCP tools if available\n    try:\n        # Get the repository root path\n        repo_root = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent.parent\n        kb_path = repo_root / \"knowledge-base\"\n        \n        # Create MCP tools for filesystem access (limited to knowledge-base directory)\n        fs_mcp = MCPTools(f\"npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem {kb_path}\")\n        tools.append(fs_mcp)\n        logger.info(\"Filesystem MCP tool initialized\")\n        \n        # Create MCP tools for database access (if DB exists)\n        db_path = repo_root / \"db\" / \"uap_research.db\"\n        if db_path.exists():\n            db_mcp = MCPTools(f\"npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-database 'sqlite:///{db_path}'\")\n            tools.append(db_mcp)\n            logger.info(f\"Database MCP tool initialized with {db_path}\")\n        \n        # Create MCP tools for HTTP access\n        http_mcp = MCPTools(f\"npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-http\")\n        tools.append(http_mcp)\n        logger.info(\"HTTP MCP tool initialized\")\n        \n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.error(f\"Error initializing MCP tools: {e}\")\n    \n    return tools",

        "contents": "\n\n/**\n * Executes an asynchronous operation with retry logic.\n * @template T\n * @param {() =\u003e Promise\u003cT\u003e} operation - The asynchronous operation to execute.\n * @param {string} actionType - A label for the action being executed.\n * @param {Record\u003cstring, any\u003e} context - Additional context for logging purposes.\n * @param {FirecrawlConfig} [config=DEFAULT_CONFIG] - Configuration for retries.\n * @returns {Promise\u003cT\u003e} The result of the operation or an error response after retries.\n */\nasync function executeWithRetry\u003cT\u003e(\n  operation: () =\u003e Promise\u003cT\u003e,\n  actionType: string,\n  context: Record\u003cstring, any\u003e,\n  config: FirecrawlConfig = DEFAULT_CONFIG\n): Promise\u003cT\u003e {\n  for (let attempt = 1; attempt \u003c= config.maxRetries; attempt++) {\n    try {\n      const result = await operation();\n      if (!result) {\n        throw new Error(&#96;${actionType} returned no data&#96;);\n      }\n      return result;\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (attempt === config.maxRetries) {\n        const errorResponse: ErrorResponse = {\n          success: false,\n          error: actionType,\n          message:\n            error instanceof Error ? error.message : \"Unknown error occurred\",\n        };\n        return errorResponse as T;\n      }\n\n   \n\n      await new Promise((resolve) =\u003e\n        setTimeout(resolve, config.retryDelay * attempt)\n      );\n    }\n  }\n\n  const errorResponse: ErrorResponse = {\n    success: false,\n    error: actionType,\n    message: \"Operation failed after max retries\",\n  };\n  return errorResponse as T;\n}",

        "originalContents": "\n\n/**\n * Executes an asynchronous operation with retry logic.\n * @template T\n * @param {() =\u003e Promise\u003cT\u003e} operation - The asynchronous operation to execute.\n * @param {string} actionType - A label for the action being executed.\n * @param {Record\u003cstring, any\u003e} context - Additional context for logging purposes.\n * @param {FirecrawlConfig} [config=DEFAULT_CONFIG] - Configuration for retries.\n * @returns {Promise\u003cT\u003e} The result of the operation or an error response after retries.\n */\nasync function executeWithRetry\u003cT\u003e(\n  operation: () =\u003e Promise\u003cT\u003e,\n  actionType: string,\n  context: Record\u003cstring, any\u003e,\n  config: FirecrawlConfig = DEFAULT_CONFIG\n): Promise\u003cT\u003e {\n  for (let attempt = 1; attempt \u003c= config.maxRetries; attempt++) {\n    try {\n      const result = await operation();\n      if (!result) {\n        throw new Error(&#96;${actionType} returned no data&#96;);\n      }\n      return result;\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (attempt === config.maxRetries) {\n        const errorResponse: ErrorResponse = {\n          success: false,\n          error: actionType,\n          message:\n            error instanceof Error ? error.message : \"Unknown error occurred\",\n        };\n        return errorResponse as T;\n      }\n\n   \n\n      await new Promise((resolve) =\u003e\n        setTimeout(resolve, config.retryDelay * attempt)\n      );\n    }\n  }\n\n  const errorResponse: ErrorResponse = {\n    success: false,\n    error: actionType,\n    message: \"Operation failed after max retries\",\n  };\n  return errorResponse as T;\n}",

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "---\ndescription: Guide for using Task Master to manage task-driven development workflows\nglobs: **/*\nalwaysApply: true\n---\n# Task Master Development Workflow\n\nThis guide outlines the typical process for using Task Master to manage software development projects.\n\n## Primary Interaction: MCP Server vs. CLI\n\nTask Master offers two primary ways to interact:\n\n1.  **MCP Server (Recommended for Integrated Tools)**:\n    - For AI agents and integrated development environments (like Cursor), interacting via the **MCP server is the preferred method**.\n    - The MCP server exposes Task Master functionality through a set of tools (e.g., &#96;get_tasks&#96;, &#96;add_subtask&#96;).\n    - This method offers better performance, structured data exchange, and richer error handling compared to CLI parsing.\n    - Refer to [&#96;mcp.mdc&#96;](mdc:.cursor/rules/mcp.mdc) for details on the MCP architecture and available tools.\n    - A comprehensive list and description of MCP tools and their corresponding CLI commands can be found in [&#96;taskmaster.mdc&#96;](mdc:.cursor/rules/taskmaster.mdc).\n    - **Restart the MCP server** if core logic in &#96;scripts/modules&#96; or MCP tool/direct function definitions change.\n\n2.  **&#96;task-master&#96; CLI (For Users \u0026 Fallback)**:\n    - The global &#96;task-master&#96; command provides a user-friendly interface for direct terminal interaction.\n    - It can also serve as a fallback if the MCP server is inaccessible or a specific function isn't exposed via MCP.\n    - Install globally with &#96;npm install -g task-master-ai&#96; or use locally via &#96;npx task-master-ai ...&#96;.\n    - The CLI commands often mirror the MCP tools (e.g., &#96;task-master list&#96; corresponds to &#96;get_tasks&#96;).\n    - Refer to [&#96;taskmaster.mdc&#96;](mdc:.cursor/rules/taskmaster.mdc) for a detailed command reference.\n\n## Standard Development Workflow Process\n\n",

        "originalContents": "---\ndescription: Guide for using Task Master to manage task-driven development workflows\nglobs: **/*\nalwaysApply: true\n---\n# Task Master Development Workflow\n\nThis guide outlines the typical process for using Task Master to manage software development projects.\n\n## Primary Interaction: MCP Server vs. CLI\n\nTask Master offers two primary ways to interact:\n\n1.  **MCP Server (Recommended for Integrated Tools)**:\n    - For AI agents and integrated development environments (like Cursor), interacting via the **MCP server is the preferred method**.\n    - The MCP server exposes Task Master functionality through a set of tools (e.g., &#96;get_tasks&#96;, &#96;add_subtask&#96;).\n    - This method offers better performance, structured data exchange, and richer error handling compared to CLI parsing.\n    - Refer to [&#96;mcp.mdc&#96;](mdc:.cursor/rules/mcp.mdc) for details on the MCP architecture and available tools.\n    - A comprehensive list and description of MCP tools and their corresponding CLI commands can be found in [&#96;taskmaster.mdc&#96;](mdc:.cursor/rules/taskmaster.mdc).\n    - **Restart the MCP server** if core logic in &#96;scripts/modules&#96; or MCP tool/direct function definitions change.\n\n2.  **&#96;task-master&#96; CLI (For Users \u0026 Fallback)**:\n    - The global &#96;task-master&#96; command provides a user-friendly interface for direct terminal interaction.\n    - It can also serve as a fallback if the MCP server is inaccessible or a specific function isn't exposed via MCP.\n    - Install globally with &#96;npm install -g task-master-ai&#96; or use locally via &#96;npx task-master-ai ...&#96;.\n    - The CLI commands often mirror the MCP tools (e.g., &#96;task-master list&#96; corresponds to &#96;get_tasks&#96;).\n    - Refer to [&#96;taskmaster.mdc&#96;](mdc:.cursor/rules/taskmaster.mdc) for a detailed command reference.\n\n## Standard Development Workflow Process\n\n",

        "contents": "class XataMCPTools {\n  constructor(private adapter: BaseDatabaseAdapter) {}\n  \n  @mcpTool('xata-query')\n  async executeQuery(params: {\n    query: string;\n    parameters?: any[];\n    consistency?: 'strong' | 'eventual';\n  }) {\n    if (this.adapter instanceof XataLiteAdapter) {\n      // HTTP API approach\n      return await this.adapter.sql({\n        statement: params.query,\n        params: params.parameters,\n        consistency: params.consistency\n      });\n    } else if (this.adapter instanceof XataPostgresAdapter) {\n      // Postgres wire approach\n      return await this.adapter.executeQuery(params.query, params.parameters);\n    }\n    \n    throw new Error('Unsupported adapter for SQL queries');\n  }\n  \n  @mcpTool('xata-search')\n  async searchContent(params: {\n    table: string;\n    query: string;\n    options?: SearchOptions;\n  }) {\n    if (this.adapter instanceof XataLiteAdapter) {\n      return await this.adapter.searchRecords(params.table, params.query, params.options);\n    }\n    \n    // Fallback to text search for Postgres\n    return await this.adapter.executeQuery(&#96;\n      SELECT * FROM ${params.table}\n      WHERE to_tsvector('english', content) @@ to_tsquery('english', $1)\n    &#96;, [params.query]);\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Web UI Integration\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Frontend integration with Xata adapters\n",

        "contents": "import { fireCrawl } from \"./firecrawl.client\";\nimport type {\n\tScrapeOptions,\n\tCrawlOptions,\n\tMapOptions,\n\tChangeTrackingOptions,\n\tDeepResearchOptions,\n} from \"./types\";\n\n/**\n * Scrape content from a URL with enhanced options\n * @param url URL to scrape\n * @param options Scrape configuration options\n * @param prompt Optional prompt for the FIRE-1 agent\n */\nexport const scrape = async (\n\turl: string,\n\toptions: ScrapeOptions = {},\n\tprompt?: string,\n) =\u003e {\n\ttry {\n\t\t// Always use FIRE-1 agent by default with optional prompt\n\t\tconst agent = { model: \"FIRE-1\", prompt: prompt || \"\" };\n\t\tconst config = { ...options, agent };\n\t\treturn await fireCrawl.scrapeUrl(url, config);\n\t} catch (error) {\n\t\tconsole.error(\"FireCrawl scrape error:\", error);\n\t\tthrow error;\n\t}\n};",

        "contents": "\n\n// Unified schema for LLM input\nexport const firecrawlInputSchema = z\n  .object({\n    action: z\n      .enum([\"scrape\", \"crawl\", \"map\"])\n      .describe(\n        \"The type of operation to perform. Capable only choose one from 'scrape', 'crawl', or 'map'.\"\n      ),\n    scrapeOptions: scrapeOptionSchema\n      .optional()\n      .describe(\n        \"Options specific to the scrape action. Required when action is 'scrape'.\"\n      ),\n    crawlOptions: crawlOptionSchema\n      .optional()\n      .describe(\n        \"Options specific to the crawl action. Required when action is 'crawl'.\"\n      ),\n    mapOptions: mapOptionSchema\n      .optional()\n      .describe(\n        \"Options specific to the map action. Required when action is 'map'.\"\n      ),\n  })\n  .refine(\n    (data) =\u003e\n      (data.action === \"scrape\" \u0026\u0026 data.scrapeOptions) ||\n      (data.action === \"crawl\" \u0026\u0026 data.crawlOptions) ||\n      (data.action === \"map\" \u0026\u0026 data.mapOptions),\n    {\n      message:\n        \"The corresponding options object (scrapeOptions, crawlOptions, or mapOptions) must be provided based on the chosen action.\",\n      path: [\"action\"],\n    }\n  );",

+ #!/usr/bin/env node
+ 
+ import { fireCrawl } from './packages/services/firecrawl/firecrawl.client.js';
+ import { writeFileSync } from 'fs';
+ import { join } from 'path';
+ 
+ async function scrapeUFOCasebook() {
+   const url = 'https://www.ufocasebook.com/casefiles.html';
+   
+   console.log(&#96;🚀 Scraping ${url}...&#96;);
+   
+   try {
+     const scrapeOptions = {
+       formats: ['markdown', 'content'],
+       onlyMainContent: true,
+       waitFor: 3000, // Wait 3 seconds for page to load
+       removeBase64Images: true, // Remove base64 images to keep file size manageable
+     };
+ 
+     const response = await fireCrawl.scrapeUrl(url, scrapeOptions);
+     
+     if (!response.success) {
+       throw new Error(&#96;Scraping failed: ${response.error || 'Unknown error'}&#96;);
+     }
+ 
+     // Generate filename with timestamp
+     const timestamp = new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, '-').split('T')[0];
+     const filename = &#96;ufocasebook-casefiles-${timestamp}.md&#96;;
+     const filepath = join(process.cwd(), filename);
+ 
+     // Prepare markdown content with metadata
+     const metadata = &#96;---
+ title: UFO Casebook - Case Files
+ url: ${url}
+ scraped_at: ${new Date().toISOString()}
+ scraper: Firecrawl
+ ---
+ 
+ # UFO Casebook - Case Files
+ 
+ Source: [${url}](${url})
+ Scraped: ${new Date().toLocaleString()}
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ &#96;;
+ 
+     const markdownContent = response.data?.markdown || response.data?.content || 'No content available';
+     const fullContent = metadata + markdownContent;
+ 
+     // Write to file
+     writeFileSync(filepath, fullContent, 'utf8');
+     
+     console.log(&#96;✅ Successfully scraped and saved to: ${filename}&#96;);
+     console.log(&#96;📄 Content length: ${markdownContent.length} characters&#96;);
+     console.log(&#96;📁 Full path: ${filepath}&#96;);
+     
+     return {
+       success: true,
+       filename,
+       filepath,
+       contentLength: markdownContent.length
+     };
+ 
+   } catch (error) {
+     console.error('❌ Scraping failed:', error.message);
+     
+     // Log more details if available
+     if (error.response) {
+       console.error('Response status:', error.response.status);
+       console.error('Response data:', error.response.data);
+     }
+     
+     throw error;
+   }
+ }
+ 
+ // Run the scraper
+ if (import.meta.url === &#96;file://${process.argv[1]}&#96;) {
+   scrapeUFOCasebook()
+     .then(result =&gt; {
+       console.log('\n🎉 Scraping completed successfully!');
+       process.exit(0);
+     })
+     .catch(error =&gt; {
+       console.error('\n💥 Scraping failed:', error.message);
+       process.exit(1);
+     });
+ }
+ 
+ export { scrapeUFOCasebook };
